text:
devin: quick dump from today's perf run — host-side preflight (token pre-stripper) is adding ~4-8ms p95 on short requests, +10-15ms p99 when combined with grpc chunking. stack: preflight_strip -> parse_headers -> stream_handoff -> http2_writev

jia: ugh, that aligns with the flamegraphs i grabbed. see snippet: `https://internal/fg/17355/preflight-strip` :eyes:

sam: can you paste the exact command you used for the perf run? trying to repro locally

devin: ran: `./perfbench --mode=ingress --qps=500 --seq=32 --payload=short` on canary host, CPU bound on host parse path. also toggled http2 window size (default) and saw more small writes.

maria: i noticed kv-cache evictions spike at same time — could be churn from pre-parsed prefixes being dropped, causing more work in `stream_handoff` to rebuild preparse state :thinking_face:

eli: quick idea: skip the preflight_strip pass for payloads < 64 bytes and stream=true. cheap guard, low risk. we saw similar win in proxy last year.

jia: can you show the prior vs post numbers if we skip? also what about grpc writev coalescing? current rpc layer issues a write per chunk sometimes.

devin: baseline p95 tokenization overhead: 6.4ms, p99 14.9ms. with preflight skip heuristic (local patch) p95 -> 2.8ms, p99 -> 6.1ms. end-to-end p99 (including grpc) dropped ~9ms. will push numbers to the doc.

sam: nice. what's the failure mode? any parsing regressions if we skip?

devin: risk is minimal for plain text payloads — we still run the main tokenizer later. preflight currently does some aggressive prefix trimming and ascii-only fastpath; skipping means more work later but avoids redundant copies + small write amplification.

maria: we should watch KV cache hit-rate. if skipping increases later parse work per request, we may thrash small cache entries. can you attach the kvcache hit-rate delta?

devin: attached sample metrics:
```
kvcache.hit_rate.before=0.62
kvcache.hit_rate.after=0.59
parse.cpu_ms.delta=+0.7ms avg
parse.allocs.delta=-1.2KB
```
overall host-side CPU drops by ~12% on short requests even with small hit-rate dip.

eli: that's acceptable to start. recommend feature-flag rollout w/ a canary group and `--preflight-skip-threshold=64` configurable. also add a metric: `preflight.skipped.count` and `preflight.skipped.kvcache_miss`

infra-bot: deploy check: canary cluster `canary-ops-3` has capacity. submit PR and set `ff=preflight_skip` to true for canary. :white_check_mark:

devin: PR posted: `github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4582` — includes bench script and perf dashboards. rolling to canary now.

jia: also noticed grpc small-write behavior — maybe bump coalesce window in rpc layer: `coalesce.max_small_writes=8` gave ~3ms gain in microbench. I'll prototype a fallback that delays first write for 200us to allow coalescing when client sends more stream frames.

sam: delaying write worries me for tail-latency. 200us is significant. maybe adaptive: only delay when seq<=32 and observed upstream burst within last 5s.

jia: yep adaptive is the plan. will couple it with an observable `rpc.coalesce_delay_ms` and circuit breaker.

maria: next steps checklist:
- monitor kvcache hit-rate & parse CPU per-route
- canary rollout of preflight skip + metric flags
- prototype rpc coalesce adaptive delay (bench first)
- add e2e smoke that validates tokenization parity on sampled requests

eli: i'll add the FF and alert hooks. Devs, tag me when PR ready for prod rollout.

devin: thanks everyone. will update thread with canary numbers in ~45m. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy started for `pr/4582` to `canary-ops-3` at 2024-07-15T18:14:22Z

devin: canary results posted: p95 host parse down from 6.4ms -> 2.9ms, p99 down 14.9ms -> 6.3ms, end-to-end p99 drop 8.7ms. no increase in error rate. leaving FF enabled for now.

maria: sweet. i'll keep an eye on kvcache panels overnight. reported to runbook channel if anything odd.

sam: nice work — let's schedule a short writeup for eng docs on the heuristic and tradeoffs.

eli: I'll follow up with rollout plan for prod after 24h canary.

devin: closing loop — thanks all.
